skill.name: wireshark-network-traffic-analysis
skill.description: Guides authorized Wireshark packet capture, display filtering, stream reconstruction, traffic statistics, and incident-focused protocol analysis for PCAP and live captures.
skill.summary: Analyze authorized network captures with Wireshark filters, streams, statistics, and security workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and Wireshark filter examples. One high-confidence issue remains: the TLS troubleshooting section directs users to obtain a server private key, which requires stronger handling guidance.

remediation.issue: TLS decryption guidance asks users to obtain a server private key.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization, prefer temporary test keys or TLS key logs, and warn users never to share private keys with AI tools.

remediation.issue: Packet captures may contain credentials, tokens, personal data, and confidential traffic.
remediation.suggestion: Add clearer guidance for PCAP storage, redaction, retention, and sharing only sanitized excerpts.

remediation.issue: Live capture workflows can be misused outside authorized networks.
remediation.suggestion: State that users must confirm scope, ownership, and approval before starting any live packet capture.

content.value_statement: Network captures can be difficult to interpret during outages and investigations. This skill guides authorized Wireshark filtering, stream review, statistics, and evidence-focused analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains capture filters and display filters for hosts, ports, protocols, TCP flags, DNS, and HTTP.
Guides TCP, UDP, HTTP, and TLS stream review in Wireshark.
Uses Wireshark statistics, conversations, endpoints, flow graphs, and I/O graphs for traffic analysis.
Provides workflows for port scan detection, ARP spoofing checks, DNS review, and malware beaconing triage.
Lists operational guardrails for authorized capture, privacy handling, and secure PCAP storage.
limitations: It does not automate packet capture or parse PCAP files without Wireshark.
Encrypted payloads remain hidden unless authorized keys or key logs are available.
Live capture can require administrator privileges and may miss packets on high-speed networks.
Findings still require validation against network context and change records.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Network Outages
use_cases.description: Review packet loss, retransmissions, connection resets, and traffic timing to isolate service or path problems.

use_cases.title: Investigate Suspicious Traffic
use_cases.description: Filter PCAP files for unusual DNS, port scanning, beaconing, plaintext credentials, and unexpected external connections.

use_cases.title: Document Incident Evidence
use_cases.description: Use streams, statistics, endpoints, and exported dissections to create clear evidence for incident timelines.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic PCAP Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a provided capture file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me review this PCAP in Wireshark. List the first filters and statistics I should check for basic triage.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Web Slowness
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through Wireshark analysis for a slow web application. Focus on retransmissions, response times, resets, and traffic volume.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Possible Malware Traffic
prompt_templates.scenario: Security investigation with suspected command and control traffic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me analyze suspected malware traffic in Wireshark. Prioritize DNS patterns, beaconing intervals, unusual ports, and endpoint summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Incident Evidence Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Wireshark workflow for preserving evidence from an authorized capture. Include filters, streams, exported views, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to investigate slow access to an internal web application.
output: Check conversations and service response time for the web server.
Filter for retransmissions, duplicate acknowledgements, resets, and zero-window events.
Compare I/O graph spikes with user-reported time ranges.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to triage a suspicious PCAP from an endpoint alert.
output: Start with protocol hierarchy, endpoints, DNS queries, and conversation summaries.
Look for regular beaconing, random-looking domains, unusual ports, and large outbound transfers.
Document any indicators with packet numbers, timestamps, and related streams.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to review plaintext credential exposure.
output: Limit analysis to authorized captures and approved systems.
Review HTTP form submissions and stream contents for exposed usernames, passwords, or tokens.
Redact sensitive values before sharing findings or reports.

best_practices: Capture only traffic you are authorized to inspect.
Use capture filters to reduce sensitive data collection.
Store PCAP files securely and redact secrets before sharing results.
anti_patterns: Do not capture third-party traffic without approval.
Do not paste credentials, tokens, private keys, or raw PCAP secrets into AI tools.
Do not treat a single packet pattern as proof without corroborating context.

faq.question: Does this skill run Wireshark automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis workflows, filters, and review steps for users operating Wireshark.

faq.question: Can it analyze encrypted traffic?
faq.answer: It can guide metadata review. Payload decryption requires authorized keys, key logs, or supported protocol settings.

faq.question: Is live packet capture covered?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains live capture setup, interface selection, filters, and operational limits.

faq.question: Can it help with incident response?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports PCAP triage, stream review, suspicious traffic detection, and evidence documentation.

faq.question: What data should users avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Users should avoid sharing credentials, tokens, private keys, personal data, and unsanitized packet captures.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for network engineers, security analysts, incident responders, and learners with authorization to inspect traffic.
